name: Academic Search Premier
purpose: Multidisciplinary database suggested for the search.
notes: Access per extraction notes (subscription or institutional). p. 6.

name: APA Meta-Analysis Reporting Standards (MARS)
purpose: Reporting standards for meta-analyses in the APA Publication Manual (6th ed.).
notes: The source cites the APA Publication Manual, 6th ed. (p. 15). Background: MARS is now part of APA's Journal Article Reporting Standards (JARS-Quant), whose tables are freely available on the APA Style website.

name: BibTeX
purpose: Reference management format/tool used for importing and deduplicating records.

name: Campbell Collaboration
purpose: Protocol registration and library of systematic reviews in the social sciences.
notes: Also the source of the MEC2IR reporting standards. p. 5, p. 15.

name: Campbell MEC2IR (Methodological Expectations of Campbell Collaboration Intervention Reviews)
purpose: Reporting standards for Campbell intervention reviews.
notes: The Campbell Collaboration (2019), Campbell Policies and Guidelines Series No. 4; the DOI is printed in the reference list. Open access. p. 15.

name: ChatGPT
purpose: General AI assistant the author used, with Claude, for limited editorial support in preparing the guide.
notes: Named only in the AI Disclosure Statement. p. 27. Access not stated in the source (general knowledge: free sign-up tier plus paid plans); 'unknown' replaced with a schema value.

name: CINAHL
purpose: Nursing and allied-health database; one of the seven key databases.
notes: p. 8. Access model not stated in the source.

name: Claude
purpose: General AI assistant the author used, with ChatGPT, for limited editorial support (language clarity, synthesis, stylistic consistency) in preparing the guide.
notes: Named only in the AI Disclosure Statement; the author retains full responsibility for content. p. 27. Access not stated in the source (general knowledge: free sign-up tier plus paid plans); 'unknown' replaced with a schema value.

name: ClinicalTrials.gov
purpose: Trial registry, searched for registered studies that were never published or never released their results; this gives direct evidence of publication bias.
notes: Ch12 p. 256. The book notes that registration is generally required for interventional (and cohort) studies before they start. The URL is from general knowledge; the book gives none.

name: Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews
purpose: Database of Cochrane reviews; Davey et al. (2011) analysed 22,453 meta-analyses from one issue (median 3 studies, maximum 294) as a benchmark for the number of studies.
notes: Mentioned only as the source of the benchmark, not as a search database. Access not stated in the source (subscription or national licence, general knowledge). p. 123.

name: Cochrane (Library)
purpose: Source of trial records (CENTRAL) searched up to April 2020; the abstract calls it 'Cochrane clinical trial center'.
notes: Protocol registration first requires registering the question with a Cochrane review group, which can be difficult for some reviewers. Background: reading full reviews may require a subscription depending on country. p. 5.

name: Cochrane risk-of-bias tool (original, RoB 1)
purpose: Risk-of-bias assessment of the 24 included RCTs across 7 domains (Higgins & Green 2011 Handbook).
notes: p. 19. The source lists the original RoB 1 domains (selection, performance, detection, attrition, reporting); current Cochrane guidance uses RoB 2, which the source does not describe.

name: Comprehensive Meta-Analysis (CMA)
purpose: Windows meta-analysis program whose output (Std diff in means, Fixed and Random summary rows, relative-weight columns per model, forest plots) illustrates the FE vs RE comparisons.
notes: Access model not stated in the source (commercial paid licence per general knowledge). The address www.Meta-Analysis.com printed on the draft's title page and footers is, per general knowledge, also the CMA vendor site. Its random-effects results in the screenshots match DerSimonian-Laird tau^2 with z-based CIs (recomputed). It displays effect/SE/variance to 3 decimals and relative weights to 2 decimals. Located pp. 90, 100, 107–108, 111, 113. [note: DL with a z CI is no longer the recommended RE default; see K-BOR07-031/032.]

name: Connected Papers
purpose: Similarity graph around one or more origin papers built from shared references and co-citation; Prior Works (likely foundational sources) and Derivative Works (later follow-ups and reviews); graph and list views.
notes: Pricing is not stated in the text; saving papers and graph history is for account holders and the screenshot shows a 'Pricing' link, implying paid tiers (p. 16). Input by title, DOI, arXiv URL, Semantic Scholar URL or PubMed URL (p. 16 scr.). Not a citation tree; position and citation counts show neither agreement nor quality; results depend on origin papers and citation data (pp. 15, 17). pp. 15–17 §7.

name: Consensus
purpose: AI academic search engine: question-driven search, Paper Search without synthesis, Pro analysis (cited synthesis), Deep Review, Consensus Meter (apparent agreement on yes/no questions), Study Snapshot, research filters, Ask Paper.
notes: Free entry tier implied by the named 'Pro analysis' feature (p. 25) but not stated; the screenshot shows only 'Sign up'/'Sign in'. Screenshot: 'Sign up', 'Sign in', 'Corpus' and 'Deep' toggles; claims 'Search & analyze 220M+ peer reviewed research papers' (p. 25 scr., marketing claim). Summaries and agreement indicators do not establish evidence quality or search completeness (p. 26). Not from the source: a Consensus MCP connector is available in this assistant's session; the same caveats apply. pp. 25–26 §12.

name: CONSORT
purpose: Minimum set of recommendations for reporting randomised controlled trials (Moher et al. 2012).
notes: Relevant for appraising primary RCT reports, not for reporting the review itself. The source cites the CONSORT 2010 explanation and elaboration (Moher et al. 2012). [note: CONSORT 2010 has been superseded by CONSORT 2025.]

name: Covidence
purpose: Review-management platform: import and deduplication, independent title/abstract screening with hidden votes, conflict management, full-text review with exclusion reasons, custom extraction forms, AI-assisted extraction with supporting quotations, screening prioritisation, quality/risk-of-bias templates, exports.
notes: Subscription or institutional licence with free trial; screenshot shows 'Free trial', 'Book a demo for your institution', 'Check if your institution already has access', 'Pricing' (p. 6 scr.). Works only after searches; does not search databases or write the synthesis (p. 5). Every AI suggestion needs verification; prioritisation still needs a human decision on every record (p. 7). pp. 5–7 §2.

name: CRAN Task View: Meta-Analysis
purpose: Curated list of R packages for meta-analysis.
notes: Dewey (2015). URL printed in the reference list. p. 126. Category set to 'software' (a catalogue of software packages).

name: CRAN Task View: MetaAnalysis
purpose: Curated overview of R packages for meta-analysis.

name: dmetar (R package)
purpose: power.analysis() for prospective random-effects power, find.outliers(), InfluenceAnalysis(), eggers.test().
notes: Harrer et al. (2021), companion to 'Doing meta-analysis with R'. Background: installed from GitHub, not on CRAN. eggers.test prints CI = intercept +/- 1.96*SE. pp. 5, 10–12.

name: EBSCO
purpose: Database platform suggested for the search.
notes: Access per extraction notes (subscription or institutional). p. 6.

name: Elicit
purpose: AI research assistant: semantic and Boolean search, customisable comparison tables, source-linked extraction, Research Reports, paper chat, review workflow (title/abstract and full-text screening, extraction, reporting), Zotero import and exports.
notes: Plan-based: exports vary by plan (p. 24). Screenshot: 'Sign up', 'Sign in', 'Pricing'; tagline 'Conduct searches across papers, web, and trials' (p. 23 scr.). Free tier not stated in the text. Tables and reports are working material; some records contain only abstracts; formal reviews need a documented search, database coverage and critical appraisal (p. 25). pp. 23–25 §11.

name: Elsevier (publisher platform)
purpose: Publisher full-text platform suggested for the search.
notes: Access per extraction notes (subscription or institutional). p. 6.

name: Embase
purpose: Biomedical bibliographic database listed as a candidate search source.
notes: Access not stated in the source (subscription or institutional, general knowledge). p. 123.

name: EndNote
purpose: Reference manager for tracking study documents, referencing, and supporting study selection.
notes: Named as an example reference database for screening (p. 13). Access model not stated in the source.

name: ERIC
purpose: Education research database; one of three sources in the growth-mindset protocol example.
notes: Protocol example (p. 5). Access model not stated in the source.

name: esc (R package)
purpose: Effect size computation; esc_f() converts F statistics to effect sizes when summary data are missing.
notes: Lüdecke (2019), version 0.5.1 cited. p. 9.

name: EThOS (British Library theses service)
purpose: UK doctoral theses database suggested for grey-literature searching.
notes: p. 8. Service disrupted since the 2023 British Library cyber-incident, so check availability (extractor's assessment).

name: GetFTR
purpose: Full-text access service connected to R Discovery so eligible users can retrieve subscribed full texts.
notes: Depends on the user's institutional subscriptions ('eligible users'). p. 22 §10.

name: Google
purpose: General web search to supplement library databases.

name: Google Scholar
purpose: Free cross-disciplinary scholarly search with citation tracking ('Cited by', 'Related articles'), full-text location ('All versions'), alerts, My Library and citation export; AI features Scholar Labs, Quick Read and Scholar PDF Reader.
notes: Explicitly called free (p. 4). My Library and alerts imply a Google account (not stated). Citation counts and AI overviews do not establish quality; use subject databases alongside it for substantial reviews (p. 5). pp. 4–5 §1.

name: GRADE
purpose: Rating the quality/certainty of a body of evidence.
notes: Balshem et al. (2011); only named in the source, without detail (p. 7). Background: the GRADE handbook and GRADEpro GDT are free for non-commercial use; GRADE is the standard for rating certainty in health reviews.

name: Hozo, Djulbegovic & Hozo (2005) conversion formulas
purpose: Estimating mean and SD from median and range when trials report medians.
notes: p. 2 §2.5. Open access in BMC Medical Research Methodology. Covers median with range only, not the IQR, although the source cites it for both; newer estimators (Wan 2014, Luo 2018, Shi 2020) perform better.

name: Jadad score (Oxford Quality Scoring System)
purpose: Quality score for RCTs from 0 (lowest) to 5 (highest) based on reported randomisation, blinding and withdrawals (Jadad et al. 1996).
notes: Described by the source as an old measure; no item-level scoring given. [note: Cochrane advises against such summary scales; prefer RoB 2.]

name: Standard Quality Assessment Criteria (Kmet et al., 2004)
purpose: Quality appraisal of primary research papers.
notes: Kmet, Lee & Cook (2004); only named in the source (p. 7). Background: published as a freely downloadable report by the Alberta Heritage Foundation for Medical Research.

name: LibKey
purpose: Library full-text linking service connected to R Discovery so eligible users can retrieve subscribed full texts.
notes: Depends on the user's institutional subscriptions ('eligible users'). p. 22 §10.

name: Linguistics Abstracts
purpose: Linguistics abstracting database suggested for the search.
notes: Access per extraction notes (subscription or institutional). p. 6.

name: SPSS meta-analysis macros (Lipsey & Wilson 2000)
purpose: Macros that run fixed-, random- and mixed-effects meta-analyses inside SPSS; used for the illustration.
notes: From Lipsey & Wilson (2000), Practical Meta-Analysis. The macros are free but need an SPSS licence (extraction notes). p. 126.

name: Litmaps
purpose: Seed-based citation mapping with citation-based and Similar Text (title/abstract) search, iterative 'More Like This', tags, BibTeX/RIS/CSV import-export, shareable maps and 'Monitor' email alerts.
notes: Free entry tier implied (advanced filters are 'paid features'), not stated; Zotero Sync only on Pro and excludes notes and attached PDFs (p. 14). Screenshot: 'Login', 'Pricing'; search by keyword, author, DOI, PubMed ID or arXiv ID (p. 14 scr.). Dense clusters do not mean strong evidence and empty areas do not mean research gaps (p. 15). pp. 13–15 §6.

name: LLBA (Linguistics and Language Behavior Abstracts)
purpose: Linguistics literature database; one of the three most used in L2 meta-analyses.
notes: Access per extraction notes (subscription or institutional). p. 6.

name: MAd (R package)
purpose: agg() aggregates dependent effect sizes within a study into one composite (Borenstein et al. 2009 method) with an assumed correlation (r = .5).
notes: Del Re & Hoyt (2010). Background: archived on CRAN; pin a version. p. 8.

name: MedCalc
purpose: Commercial statistics package; mentioned only as the source (its website) of the chapter's 8-study correlation example data.
notes: Not used for any analysis in the chapter; the data look like a teaching or fictitious example.

name: MEDLINE
purpose: Biomedical bibliographic database; one of the guide's 'seven key databases'.
notes: Free via PubMed; also available on subscription platforms. Access not stated in the source (general knowledge). p. 123.

name: Mendeley
purpose: Importing search results, removing duplicates and managing references before screening.
notes: Access model not stated in the source (general knowledge). Automatic synchronisation from R Discovery requires Prime. p. 22 §10.

name: meta (R package)
purpose: metagen() random-effects pooling, forest() forest plots, funnel() contour-enhanced funnel plots, trimfill() trim-and-fill.
notes: Schwarzer (2015, version 4.2-0 cited). Source uses comb.random = TRUE with REML and Q-profile CI. Background: in meta 5.0 and later comb.random was renamed random and REML became the default tau^2 estimator (earlier DL). pp. 10–12.

name: Introduction to Meta-Analysis book web site (www.Meta-Analysis.com)
purpose: Downloads of the Excel spreadsheets and data files for the three worked-example datasets and all computations, plus supplementary course materials and exercises.
notes: Free download as described in 2009; current availability unknown. The address is printed without a protocol prefix.

name: Meta-Analyst
purpose: Software for meta-analysis of binary, continuous and diagnostic data, cited among software reviews.
notes: Wallace et al. (2009); only cited, not used in the illustration. Access per general knowledge (extraction notes), not stated in the source. p. 126 and references.

name: metabias (Stata user-written package)
purpose: Funnel-asymmetry tests in Stata: metabias es se, begg | egger. With 2x2 counts (metabias event_treat noevent_treat event_ctrl noevent_ctrl, ...) it also runs harbord | peters.
notes: Ch12 App. A12.6. Harbord and Peters need the raw 2x2 counts, so they were not estimable for the fibrinolysis data. The book's Begg p-values match the version without continuity correction. [note: the Cochrane Handbook v6 prefers the Harbord or Peters test to Egger's for odds ratios and does not recommend Begg's test.]

name: MetaEasy (Excel add-in)
purpose: Meta-analysis add-in for Microsoft Excel.
notes: Kontopantelis & Reeves (2009). Access per extraction notes. p. 10.

name: metafor (R package)
purpose: Main meta-analysis package; rma() for random-effects models and mixed-effects meta-regression (mods = ~ x, factor() for categorical moderators).
notes: Viechtbauer (2010). The example meta-regressions use method = 'DL' with t/F (Knapp-Hartung) tests. Background: rma() defaults to REML with z tests. pp. 10, 14–15.

name: metafunnel (Stata user-written package)
purpose: Funnel plots in Stata: ssc install metafunnel, then metafunnel es se.
notes: Ch12 App. A12.3. Funnel plots are not recommended with fewer than 10 studies or for proportion meta-analyses.

name: metan (Stata command)
purpose: User-written Stata command for inverse-variance fixed-effect and random-effects meta-analysis with forest plots; Appendix 10 pools the Fisher z values (metan Z seZ, fixed|random lcols(Study) ...).
notes: Not named in the source; inferred [EXTERNAL]. Defaults: random = DL, SMD = Cohen's d (hedges and glass options), z-based CIs, no prediction interval unless rfdist is requested. [note: these defaults are outdated for new analyses; prefer REML/PM, Hedges' g, HKSJ and a prediction interval.]

name: metaninf (Stata user-written package)
purpose: Leave-one-out influence analysis in Stata.
notes: Not named in the source; inferred [EXTERNAL] from the planned leave-one-out sensitivity analysis (p. 2 §2.5), whose results are not reported.

name: metaSEM (R package)
purpose: R package for meta-analysis via structural equation modelling, including multivariate and three-level meta-analysis; produced all numeric results reported in the paper.
notes: Cheung (2015b); written by the paper's first author. The authors warn other packages may give slightly different results because of estimation methods. External knowledge (extraction notes): meta() uses ML by default via OpenMx, reml() gives REML, and CIs are Wald z by default. p. 126.

name: MetaWin
purpose: Commercial meta-analysis program.
notes: Rosenberg et al. (2000), version 2 cited. p. 10.

name: MetaXL
purpose: Microsoft Excel add-in (EpiGear) used throughout the chapter to reproduce the hand calculations: fixed-effect ('IV'), DerSimonian–Laird random-effects ('RE') and inverse-variance heterogeneity ('IVhet') meta-analysis of OR via =MAInputTable(title,"NumOR",model,range), subgroup analysis via =MASubGroups(label,output_cell,membership_range), forest plots (OR or ln OR axis), funnel plots and Doi plots with the LFK index.
notes: Free download per the book's preface (preface not in this chunk); requires Microsoft Excel. Syntax: =MAInputTable("<title>","NumRR","IV|RE|IVhet",<range>); =MASubGroups("<name>",<cell with overall analysis>,<grouping table range>). In this chunk it is used only with Wald z CIs and DL tau2; it estimates a separate DL tau2 within each subgroup (inferred) and prints no between-subgroup test. The funnel plot and the Doi plot with the LFK index come with any model run. Lets the user choose the constant added to zero cells (0.5 among others). Publisher (EpiGear) and its quality-effects option are outside knowledge. Located Ch3 p. 48; Ch4 pp. 63, 71, 77–79, 83–84.

name: Microsoft Excel
purpose: Spreadsheet used by the book for all worked-example computations; the function =NORMSDIST(Z) gives the standard normal CDF for the p-values of eqs 11.9-11.10 and 12.13-12.14.
notes: Layout: rows 3–8 studies, row 9 sums; FE block F13–F20, tau^2 block H13–H17, RE block M13–M20 (pp. 92, 102–104). Uses legacy NORMDIST(x,0,1,TRUE) (now NORM.S.DIST(x,TRUE)) and fixed 1.96; displayed rounding can hide precision (tau^2 0.039786 shown as 0.040). Access model not stated in the source.

name: MIX (Excel add-in)
purpose: Meta-analysis within Microsoft Excel.
notes: Bax et al. (2006); the cited paper's title describes MIX as free software. Access is left 'unknown' because later MIX versions were sold under a paid licence (background). p. 10.

name: MLA International Bibliography
purpose: Language and literature database suggested for the search.
notes: Access per extraction notes (subscription or institutional). p. 6.

name: MLwiN
purpose: Multilevel modelling package; Table 13.6 lists it with Stata as software that can fit the REMR dose-response model.
notes: Ch13 Table 13.6 p. 280; no code is given. Access is not stated in the book; from general knowledge it is free for UK academics and otherwise needs a paid licence.

name: MOOSE
purpose: Checklist for reporting meta-analyses of observational studies in epidemiology (Stroup et al. 2000), covering background, search strategy, methods, results, discussion and conclusion.
notes: p. 10 mis-attributes it to 'Moher et al. 2000'; the correct citation (p. 11) is Stroup et al. 2000.

name: Mplus
purpose: Structural equation modelling program used to fit meta-analyses as SEMs (Cheung 2015a, Ch. 9) for the illustration.
notes: Access model from the extraction notes (paid licence), not stated in the source. p. 126.

name: Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS)
purpose: Quality assessment of non-randomised case-control and cohort studies (selection, comparability, outcome or exposure).
notes: Wells et al. (2011); only named in the source. Access per general availability of the scale (not stated in the source). p. 7.

name: OpenGrey
purpose: Grey-literature database suggested for 'expansive' searches.
notes: p. 8. As far as the extractor knows it was archived or discontinued around 2020, so check availability before relying on it.

name: Origin (OriginLab Corporation)
purpose: Graphing software also usable for extracting data from graphs.
notes: Access model not stated in the source (commercial licence per extraction notes). p. 9.

name: Open Science Framework (OSF)
purpose: Sharing the tutorial's data set and R scripts for reproducibility.
notes: The printed URL is the tutorial's own project page. p. 1, p. 7, p. 16.

name: PRISMA 2009 (explanation and elaboration, Liberati et al. 2009)
purpose: Minimum evidence-based set of items for reporting systematic reviews and meta-analyses (Moher et al. 2009), with a flow diagram (Fig. 1.1 uses its layout).
notes: The source cites only the 2009 statement; PRISMA 2020 is not mentioned. Focused on reviews of randomised trials but usable for other intervention reviews. [note: superseded by PRISMA 2020 (Page et al. 2021); use PRISMA 2020 for new reviews.]

name: PRISMA 2020 statement (checklist and flow diagram)
purpose: Reporting guideline for systematic reviews: 27-item checklist with an Explanation and Elaboration document, plus a study-selection flow diagram.
notes: pp. 6–17. The guide quotes PRISMA 2020 items 5–9 (unnumbered) but its example flow diagram (Białek et al. 2023, p. 16) follows the older 2009 layout.

name: PRISMA-P
purpose: Reporting items for systematic-review and meta-analysis protocols (Moher et al. 2015).
notes: p. 10 mis-cites it as 'Moher et al. 2009 ... published in 2015'; p. 11 gives Moher et al. 2015. The source does not mention protocol registration (e.g. PROSPERO).

name: ProQuest Dissertations & Theses
purpose: Searching unpublished dissertations to reduce publication bias.
notes: Access per extraction notes. p. 6.

name: PROSPERO (International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews)
purpose: Protocol registration for reviews related to health and social care.
notes: No fee and no prior title registration with a review group is required. p. 5.

name: APA PsycArticles
purpose: Full-text psychology journal database; one of the seven key databases.
notes: p. 8. Subscription or institutional access (extractor's assessment).

name: Psych File Drawer
purpose: Repository of unpublished and replication studies, searched to reduce publication bias.

name: Psychology and Behavioral Sciences Collection
purpose: Psychology and behavioural-science full-text database; one of the seven key databases.
notes: p. 8. EBSCO subscription (extractor's assessment).

name: PsycINFO
purpose: Psychology abstracts database; in the seven key databases, the growth-mindset protocol and the Hofmann et al. search.
notes: Access not stated in the source (subscription or institutional, general knowledge). p. 123.

name: PubMed
purpose: Biomedical bibliographic database; used in the growth-mindset protocol and in the Hofmann et al. (2010) search example.
notes: p. 2 §2.1. [EXTERNAL] PubMed processes Boolean operators left to right, so the source's unparenthesised search string would not run as intended.

name: QUADAS-2
purpose: Risk of bias and applicability in diagnostic accuracy studies (patient selection, index test, reference standard, flow and timing).

name: QUOROM statement
purpose: Standards for reporting meta-analyses of RCTs (Moher et al. 1999): statement, checklist and flow diagram; predecessor of PRISMA.
notes: Historical; superseded by PRISMA.

name: R
purpose: Statistical computing environment hosting many meta-analysis packages, including metaSEM.
notes: The book names no specific package. [note: the note-taker, not the book, verified these equivalents: metafor rma(..., mods = ~x, method = 'DL', test = 'knha') = Stata metareg ... mm; metafor regtest(model = 'lm', predictor = 'sei') = classical Egger; metafor ranktest(exact = FALSE) = Begg as printed (the default exact test gives 0.534, not 0.51, for magnesium); metasens lfkindex = LFK.]

name: R Discovery
purpose: Current-awareness and reading tool (web, mobile, Chrome extension): search with saved searches, Ask R Discovery, personalised feeds, alerts, Chat PDF, paper previews, shareable reading lists, export to Zotero and Mendeley, institutional full text via GetFTR and LibKey.
notes: Free entry tier implied by the Prime tier and the '3/3 uses left' quota, not stated; Prime subscription adds audio, translation into more than 30 languages and automatic reference-manager sync (p. 22). Screenshot: 'Sign In', 'by Editage', AI-assistant quota '3/3 uses left' (p. 22 scr.). Feeds cannot establish that a literature search is complete; check answers, summaries and translations against originals (p. 23). pp. 21–23 §10.

name: Rayyan
purpose: Collaborative screening platform: multi-format import, duplicate detection (manual or rule-based), Include/Exclude/Maybe with labels and exclusion reasons, blind screening, conflict flags, relevance ranking, full-text screening, structured extraction and risk-of-bias recording, PRISMA flow diagrams.
notes: Freemium plus paid/institutional tiers (screenshot: 'Start For Free', 'Contact Sales', 'Enterprise', 'Pricing', p. 10). ResearchPilot AI only on eligible institutional plans; PRISMA flow diagrams on supported plans (p. 11). Works after database searching; relevance rankings do not determine eligibility; AI output needs human verification (p. 11). pp. 10–11 §4.

name: ResearchRabbit
purpose: Seed-based discovery through interactive citation maps (backward/forward), similar-paper recommendations, author networks, collections, shared collections, BibTeX/RIS/CSV import-export and alerts.
notes: Screenshot: 'Sign up – it's free' (p. 18). Paid ResearchRabbit+ adds 'Signals' research-integrity alerts; paid filters include keywords, dates, open access, retractions and journal metrics (p. 19). Zotero connection mostly an importer. Maps do not establish quality, agreement or search completeness; recommendations depend on seeds and citation data (p. 19). pp. 18–19 §8.

name: RevMan 5.0 (Review Manager)
purpose: The Cochrane Collaboration's review-writing and meta-analysis software, reviewed in Ch44 (p. 398).
notes: Listed in the Contents only; text NOT IN SAMPLE. Per the extraction notes it was free for Cochrane and academic use (not printed in the sample); version 5.0 is historical. Current RevMan (web) licensing differs from RevMan 5.0 and should be checked on the Cochrane site.

name: ROBINS-I
purpose: Risk of bias in non-randomised studies of interventions (confounding, selection, classification of interventions, deviations, missing data, outcome measurement, selection of reported result).
notes: Particularly useful when a systematic review includes non-randomised studies.

name: RREst_trend (Excel macro, P. N. Lee)
purpose: Excel macro add-in that re-expresses category-specific risk estimates against a common reference when some studies' reference category is not the lowest, before dose-response meta-analysis.
notes: Ch13 p. 279. A manual is available on the same web page. The book says only that the macro can be downloaded; 'free' comes from the extraction notes.

name: SAS
purpose: General statistics package with meta-analysis macros (van Houwelingen et al., 2002).
notes: Ch13 Table 13.6 p. 280; no code is given.

name: Scholarcy
purpose: AI reading and organisation tool producing structured summary cards, literature matrices, reference extraction (RIS/BibTeX) and exports to Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Markdown and reference managers.
notes: Freemium per screenshot ('Start Free', 'Pricing', 'Login', p. 8 scr.). Summaries are reading guides only; check claims, methods, limitations and citation details against the originals and read the original abstract before setting a study aside (pp. 8–9). pp. 7–9 §3.

name: SciSpace
purpose: AI research platform: search with tabular results, Deep Review synthesis, Chat with PDF, data-extraction tables, multilingual extraction, Research Agent, library with Zotero import, citation formatting, writing support, browser extension.
notes: Freemium with API per screenshot ('Sign up for free', 'Pricing', 'Enterprise', 'API', 'Lite' mode; claims 'Trusted by 9.6 Million+ Researchers', p. 20 scr., marketing claim). Generated reviews and tables need verification; a Deep Review does not complete a systematic-review process; formatted references need metadata checks; its AI detector is not proof of authorship or misconduct (p. 21). pp. 19–21 §9.

name: Scite
purpose: Citation-context analysis: Smart Citations (supporting/contrasting/mentioning with surrounding passage), citation reports, Scite Assistant, citation-statement search over indexed full text, Reference Check for retractions and editorial notices, collections and alerts, browser extension, Zotero integration.
notes: Subscription with free trial per screenshot ('Start Free Trial', 'Pricing'); screenshot also advertises 'Try our MCP' and claims it reads across 319M+ full-text articles (p. 12 scr., marketing claim). Classifications are prompts for closer reading, not proof, and do not establish quality; coverage depends on its index (p. 13). pp. 11–13 §5.

name: Scopus
purpose: Multidisciplinary citation and abstract database suggested for the search.
notes: Access not stated in the source (subscription or institutional, general knowledge). p. 123.

name: SocINDEX with Full Text
purpose: Sociology database; one of the seven key databases.
notes: p. 8. EBSCO subscription (extractor's assessment).

name: IBM SPSS Statistics
purpose: Statistical package in which the Lipsey & Wilson meta-analysis macros were run for the illustration.
notes: Access model from the extraction notes (paid licence), not stated in the source. p. 126.

name: Stata 10.0 with user-written meta-analysis macros
purpose: Statistical package used for every worked example in Ch 11–13: IVhet meta-analysis, robust and classical meta-regression, funnel/Doi plots and asymmetry tests, and GLST/REMR dose-response meta-analysis with restricted cubic splines (built-in mkspline, regress, test).
notes: The book does not state access models; the paid licence and free SSC packages are general knowledge. Robust SEs are HC1 (N/(N-k)), and cluster-robust SEs use G/(G-1)*(N-1)/(N-k) with G-1 df. eform output prints SE(exp b) = exp(b)*SE(b). mkspline nk(3) default knots do not reproduce the book's DRMA results.

name: admetan (Stata command)
purpose: User-written Stata command for meta-analysis: computes mean differences from six arm-level columns (n, mean, SD per arm) with the wmd option and pools them under fixed effect (default), random effects (re) or IVhet (ivhet), with subgroups via by().
notes: admetan itself is free via 'ssc install admetan' but needs a paid Stata licence (access aligned with the KHN05 seed, which shares this tool_id). The appendix data tables name columns 'TrNon-cases'/'ConNon-cases', which are illegal Stata names and must be renamed. The book prints no Stata output. Outside knowledge: model(random) defaults to DerSimonian-Laird, and admetan has since been folded into metan v4. Located Ch4 Appendix A4.2/A4.4, pp. 85–86.

name: confunnel (Stata command)
purpose: Contour-enhanced funnel plots in Stata (confunnel es se), shading significance regions p < 0.01, < 0.05 and < 0.10.
notes: Ch12 App. A12.4; installed with ssc install confunnel. For 2x2 data the book first runs admetan and then calls confunnel on the generated effect sizes and SEs. The contours are centred on the null effect.

name: forestplot (Stata command)
purpose: User-written Stata command that draws a forest plot from variables holding estimates and CI limits; Appendix 10 uses it to plot back-transformed correlations (forestplot r lb ub, nonull effect("Correlation") rcol(n) leftjustify).
notes: Needs _USE and _LABELS variables prepared by hand. The printed code plots the original r column rather than the generated es, which works only because tanh(_ES) equals r for each study.

name: glst (Stata command)
purpose: Generalised least squares for trend (GLST) dose-response meta-analysis: glst logrr doses*, cov(person_years cases) se(se) pfirst(id studytype) r|f. Without pfirst, with the ir, ci or cc option, it fits a single study.
notes: Installed with ssc install glst. Needs cases and group sizes for the covariance, and study type coded 1 = case-control, 2 = cohort with incidence rate, 3 = cohort with cumulative incidence. The reference row must come first and rows must be sorted by dose. No constant, so it cannot model absolute means or prevalences.

name: lfk (Stata command)
purpose: Draws the Doi plot and computes the LFK asymmetry index in Stata: ssc install lfk, then lfk es se.
notes: Ch12 App. A12.5. The method comes from the chapter authors' group. The LFK value depends on the zero-cell correction used (magnesium: -10.09 with 1.0 versus -10.27 with 0.5). Installed from SSC (Boston College), per the book. [note: the cut-offs are heuristic, and the LFK index is not a Cochrane-endorsed test; use it alongside, not instead of, the contour-enhanced funnel and an appropriate regression test.]

name: metaprop_one (Stata command)
purpose: User-written Stata command (ssc install metaprop_one) for meta-analysis of one proportion: metaprop_one Cases N, ftt fixed|random lcols(Studyname), with ftt = Freeman–Tukey double-arcsine transformation and second(random|fixed) to add the other model's pooled line.
notes: Free from SSC but needs a Stata licence. The book's hand calculations use the raw proportion while this command (with ftt) uses a transformed scale, so results will not match the hand calculations exactly.

name: metareg (Stata command)
purpose: User-written Stata command for classical random-effects meta-regression (Harbord & Higgins 2008): metareg _ES chol_reduc, wsse(_seES) eform graph mm.
notes: The mm option gives a method-of-moments residual tau^2, and Knapp–Hartung t-tests are applied by default. Output includes tau2_res, I2_res ('% residual variation due to heterogeneity') and an adjusted R^2 based on tau^2. Recomputation shows it equals metafor rma(method='DL', test='knha').

name: xblc (Stata command)
purpose: Turns spline coefficients into dose-specific effects (RR or MD with CI) at chosen doses and plots the pooled dose-response curve: xblc doses*, covname(dose) at(levels) [ref(0)] eform line.
notes: Installed with net install st0215_1. CIs are z-based. Predictions include the constant when the model has one (REMR), so the REMR RR at dose 0 is 0.95, not 1. GLST needs ref(0) because it has no constant.

name: Standard normal and chi-squared tables
purpose: Printed tables used in the chapter's hand calculations to obtain P values for the z and Q statistics.
notes: Table look-up only brackets the p-value (Q = 14.15 with df = 7 gives p between 0.025 and 0.05 against the 5% critical value 14.067; exact p = 0.0485); prefer exact values (engine: distributions.chi2_sf, distributions.z_two_sided_p).

name: STROBE
purpose: Reporting guideline for observational studies; adherence is coded as a study characteristic.
notes: Named only as a coding item (p. 18).

name: Thalheimer & Cook (2002) effect-size calculation guide
purpose: Simplified methodology and formulas for calculating effect sizes from published statistics.
notes: Cited with Lipsey & Wilson (2001) as a source of conversion formulas. p. 9.

name: Web of Science
purpose: Citation/bibliographic database for literature searches (named 'ISI' in the source).
notes: p. 2 §2.1. Subscription or institutional access (access model from the extraction notes). The source spells it 'Web of Sciences'.

name: WebPlotDigitizer
purpose: Extracts numerical data (means, SDs) from published graphs when they are not reported in text or tables.
notes: Rohatgi (2021), version 4.5 cited. p. 9.

name: Wiley Online Library
purpose: Publisher full-text platform suggested for the search.
notes: Access per extraction notes (subscription or institutional). p. 6.

name: D. B. Wilson's web-based effect-size calculator (Campbell Collaboration)
purpose: Online calculator for converting reported statistics (t, F, p etc.) to effect sizes.
notes: Suggested instead of manual computation. p. 9.

name: WorldCat
purpose: Global library catalogue suggested for grey-literature searching (books, theses, reports).
notes: p. 8. Access model not stated in the source.

name: Zotero
purpose: Reference manager named as the import/export/sync target of Scholarcy, Scite, Litmaps, ResearchRabbit, SciSpace, R Discovery and Elicit.
notes: Access model not stated in the source (general knowledge). Litmaps Zotero Sync is Pro-only and excludes notes and attached PDFs (p. 14); ResearchRabbit's Zotero connection works mainly as an importer (p. 19); R Discovery auto-sync requires Prime (p. 22). pp. 8, 12, 14, 19, 20, 22, 24.
